issue.title: Dynamic configuration of lobby
issue.body:
There are many runtime parameters that are currently statically hardcoded in [`src/main/config`](https://github.com/beyond-all-reason/bar-lobby/tree/7d56252c3d583acb2a95694433ca4c4b075f0dc2/src/main). Changing any of them will require re-release of new version of lobby which is very suboptimal as they might change way more often then lobby codebase.

The values being hardcoded in code also might make it also harder for local development, or connecting to different stacks of infrastructure with the same lobby (e.g. prod and integration teiserver), so it would be good to be able to override those configurations without rebuild.

The issue here is to implement mechanism similar to the one in https://github.com/beyond-all-reason/spring-launcher:
- Dynamic configuration via JSON file
- Updates of the configuration from remote url
- Ability to override config via command line flag

In addition:
- Configuration needs to be described by JSON schema

timeline.body:
639831274f02db63f8e5668417b3f1bdf95d5b34
chore: Implement schema-based configuration versioning with GitHub Actions

This commit introduces a robust configuration management system with automatic schema versioning:

- Removed complex schema hash generation from application code
- Added schema versioning based on direct file hashing during CI/CD
- Implemented two GitHub Actions workflows:
  1. Schema compatibility check for PRs to ensure configs are updated when schema changes
  2. Configuration publishing workflow for deploying to dev/staging/prod environments
- Set placeholder schemaVersion in default config that gets replaced during build
- Fixed TypeScript type imports for Zod schemas
- Added npm caching to speed up CI/CD processes

The new approach simplifies schema versioning by generating a hash directly from the schema file
during the build process, rather than maintaining complex hashing logic in the application code.
This ensures that schema versions only change when the actual schema structure changes.

The GitHub Actions workflows enforce schema compatibility across environments and automate
the configuration publishing process, making it easier to manage configuration changes
across different environments.

Closes #291

Config Service Added (#597)

Closes #291 #293 #596 

This enables us to reconfigure some values without requiring an entire release of the client. Upon initialization, the client will attempt to handle 4 possible sources of config information and apply them in a cascading fashion. The first will be our remote config service, which will be updated with `remoteConfig/config.json` on a push to `master`.
